Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the switch statement within the showBug method. The switch statement only has two branches (case 1 and default), which is considered too few to demonstrate a more complex use of switch statements.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test cases call the showBug method with different inputs (1, 2, and 3). Since the switch statement in the showBug method only has two branches (case 1 and default), the test cases that trigger the default case (inputs 2 and 3) will pass, but the test cases highlight the lack of additional branches, thus triggering the bug rule 'TooFewBranchesForASwitchStatement'.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results indicate that all three tests passed successfully without any failures. This does not provide evidence that the bug 'TooFewBranchesForASwitchStatement' was triggered, as the test results only confirm that the method behaves as expected for the given inputs.
